newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS-Russia to issue more Eurobonds.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Russia to issue more Eurobonds.

text.p: Russia, encouraged by heavy oversubscribtion to its mark Eurobond, plans to make two more issues this year and to issue a rouble-denominated Eurobond next year, Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Friday.

Russia raised two billion marks ($1.2 billion) on Thursday in its second international bond issue of a seven-year Eurobond. It was priced to yield 3.70 basic points over German government bonds and will pay an annual interest rate of nine percent.
"Two billion for a debut is an absolute record -- Russia is worthy of it," Livshits told a news conference. "We are proud of it. To take a good place on this market is a big deal for a country."
Livshits said the government was considering raising at least $2 billion more through international issues.
One issue will be dollar-denominated, while the denomination of the other one was not yet decided, he said.
Russia would also create a new sector by issuing a rouble Eurobond, Livshits said.
"We shall issue the rouble paper, and people will buy it as they buy dollar paper," he said.
The rouble is not yet a fully convertible currency, but Livshits said the problem would soon be resolved.
"We shall fill in the gap within a year," he said. "It is my dream."
He also said Russia would apply for improved credit ratings.
Moody's assigned Russia's sovereign debt a Ba2 rating, Standards & Poor's gave BB minus and IBCA gave BB plus.
"We have the right to get a better rating than Ba2," Livshits said.
The mark bond followed Russia's $1.0 billion debut Eurobond, which was placed in November at 3.45 b.p.
